tellings.difference: Told first-hand, dated October 14, 2003, hovering about 45 seconds over the entry control point (not the runway) with five witnesses, then leaving at great speed.

as_told.title: Football-field-sized triangle over entry control point at Vandenberg

plain: A huge black triangular craft is said to have come in from the Pacific and hovered over Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. Jeff Natelli, who guarded nuclear missiles there, says he saw to it himself. He tells Michels that on 14 October 2003 he arrived on the scene and found five shaken witnesses. They described "a massive triangular craft larger than a football field" that "hovered silently for about 45 seconds over their entry control point," the gate where people enter, "before shooting away at impossible speed." A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown repeats the story on another episode, crediting Natelli and describing "a big black triangle coming out of the Pacific Ocean flying into Vandenberg." In Brown's version the craft is over the base's runway, while Natelli puts it over the gate. If true, it would mean something nobody could identify moved freely over one of America's most closely guarded military sites.
